item.title: Blockchain-Based Operating Systems and the Application of AI-Enabled Complexity Management in Organizations
item.content:encoded:
Ilan Alon, Ariel University

Marcin Wątorek, Cracow University of Technology

Aušrinė Šilenskytė, University of Vaasa

Ziaul Haque Munim, University of South-Eastern Norway

Organizations increasingly manage distributed decision-making and systemic complexity through blockchain technologies that function as operating systems by embedding governance mechanisms into digital infrastructures. These systems are being advanced with artificial intelligence to monitor and shape behavior. Despite blockchain-based operating systems being adopted in platforms, supply chains, and decentralized autonomous organizations, their implications for organizational administration, governance, and control remain poorly understood.

This special issue invites research that advances administrative and organizational understanding of blockchain-based operating systems with AI-enabled complexity. The call welcomes theoretically grounded, methodologically rigorous contributions including empirical studies and theory-building papers that offer clear organizational insights and engage meaningfully with blockchain and AI as organizational infrastructures.

Appel publié par Canadian Journal of Administrative Sciences / Revue Canadienne des Sciences de l Administration. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Blockchain as an organizational operating system and potential of AI advancements in it
  • Public, private, and hybrid organizations adopting blockchain OS with AI advancements
  • Integration of AI on Blockchain OS in crowdsourcing platforms, crypto exchanges, fintech firms, energy management, and transport services etc.
  • Organizational decision-making in blockchain-based and AI enabled systems
  • AI's role in administrative functions embedded in smart contracts and protocols
  • Token-based incentives as administrative and managerial mechanisms
  • Strategic control and accountability in decentralized platforms with AI-enabled advancements
  • AI integration in governance, coordination, and control without centralized authority (DAOs)
  • Complexity, emergence, and adaptation in blockchain-based and AI enabled organizations
  • Organizational legitimacy, regulation, and institutional alignment in AI and blockchain OS integrations
  • Ethical, responsible, and sustainable administration of blockchain systems, especially those advanced with AI

Timeline

  • November 15, 2026: Submission Deadline

item.title: Collaborative Intelligence in Operations Research: Models, Methods, and Applications
item.content:encoded:
Olga Battaïa, Kedge Business School

Yasser Dessouky, San Jose State University

Reza Zanjirani Farahani, Paris School of Business

Masood Fathi, University of Skövde

Madjid Tavana, La Salle University

Modern operations research increasingly demands approaches that combine human expertise with artificial intelligence and distributed problem-solving capabilities. This special issue seeks research that explores how collaborative intelligence—the synergy between human decision-makers, AI-driven systems, and mathematical optimization—can address the complexity, uncertainty, and dynamic nature of contemporary operational challenges.

The issue welcomes contributions spanning theoretical models, computational algorithms, and practical applications that demonstrate how human-AI collaboration, multi-agent coordination, decentralized optimization, and machine learning can enhance decision-making and system resilience. Submissions should showcase both rigorous mathematical foundations and real-world relevance, emphasizing the transformative potential of collaborative approaches in logistics, production, service systems, emergency response, and other complex operational environments.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Human-AI collaboration in OR models
  • Designing OR models for human decision-maker and AI agent interaction
  • Integrating human judgment, preferences, and ethical considerations into AI-driven decision-making
  • Visualizing and interpreting AI outputs
  • Optimization algorithms for multi-agent systems
  • Game-theoretic frameworks for multi-agent coordination
  • Multi-agent decision-making with diverse objectives and capabilities
  • Conflict and uncertainty management in multi-agent systems
  • Adaptive OR frameworks
  • Decentralized optimization algorithms
  • Online learning and adaptive control techniques
  • Machine learning and data analytics for OR
  • Learning-based optimization algorithms
  • Predictive analytics and simulation for decision-making
  • Risk management
  • Resilience planning
  • Distributed problem-solving

Timeline

  • December 31, 2026: Submission deadline
